clue.text: One blooming sailor I found in Liverpool's just docked

indicators.note: the sailor and I are found inside the shortened Liverpool word
docked means cut short, so just the tail letter is lopped off

parts.note: Scouse is the dialect and speech of Liverpool
AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman finds a flowering plant in Liverpool, where his ship has only just tied up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' suggests a ship tying up, but here it means cut short. Scouse is Liverpool's local speech, and a Liverpudlian is a Scouser.
explanation.definitionFit: Scabious is a flowering plant of meadows, so it is one thing that blooms.

clue.text: Statehouse seal, item for sale I picked up

parts.note: to cap a bottle is to seal it

indicators.note: in a down entry picked up means lifted, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lot is an item put up at auction

explanation.surface: An auction buyer picks up a seal for the statehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'picked up' means read from the bottom up. A capitol is a US state's legislature building.
explanation.definitionFit: A capitol is the building where a US state legislature sits.

clue.text: Old French colony Whig orator detailed in a couple of notes

indicators.note: de-tailed, with the last letter removed

parts.note: Edmund Burke was a famous Whig orator and statesman
taken as written
taken as written
fa is a note of the sol-fa scale
so, or soh, is the next note of the scale

explanation.surface: A Whig speaker is described at length in a pair of notes about a former colony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' reads as 'described closely' but means cut off the tail, so BURKE loses its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Burkina Faso in West Africa was formerly the French colony of Upper Volta.

clue.text: Nothing to salute in camp?

parts.note: O, the zero shape, is nothing
a flag is a thing to salute

explanation.surface: In the camp there is no banner to salute.
explanation.walkthrough: An oflag was a German prisoner-of-war camp for officers in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: An oflag was a wartime German prison camp holding captured officers.

clue.text: Dexterity, carving Vivien in stone

indicators.note: the actress's surname goes inside the stone abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds
Vivien Leigh was the actress who played Scarlett O'Hara

explanation.surface: Skilful hands are needed to sculpt a likeness of the actress in stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carving' looks like the sculptor's work but is only a link; a stone is a British unit of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is skill or nimbleness of hand, as in sleight of hand.

clue.text: Merciful shade covers chap

indicators.note: one word covers the other, wrapping round it on both sides

parts.note: a shade is a hue, a tint of colour
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A kindly colour scheme is said to hide a fellow from view.
explanation.definitionFit: Humane and merciful are synonyms, both describing compassion toward others.

clue.text: Working happily to secure dream of a wife

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Contentedly labouring to make a wife's dream secure.
explanation.walkthrough: Hippolyta, Queen of the Amazons, is wife-to-be of Theseus in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippolyta appears in Shakespeare's Dream as the Amazon queen betrothed to Theseus.

clue.text: Ruin most of the planet

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: Mars is the planet, the fourth from the Sun

explanation.surface: Wreck nearly the whole world.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to spoil or ruin it.

clue.text: Queen in apparently empty part of country?

indicators.note: the queen's letter goes inside the phrase meaning empty

parts.note: a place apparently empty has no folk in it
R, for Regina, is Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A monarch stays in a seemingly deserted region.
explanation.walkthrough: Norfolk, an English county, has a reputation for being flat and thinly peopled, hence 'apparently' empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Norfolk is a county of eastern England, a part of the country.

clue.text: Insect appearing enraged with penguin

parts.note: someone purple with rage is enraged, the face flushing dark
the emperor is the largest species of penguin

explanation.surface: Some bug shows up alongside an angry penguin.
explanation.walkthrough: The purple emperor is a large British butterfly; 'appearing' and 'with' just join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The purple emperor is a woodland butterfly, an example of an insect.

clue.text: Way to circle tier

parts.note: ST, street, is a way or road
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: A road loops round a stacked layer of seating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tier' is read not as a layer but as 'one that ties'.
explanation.definitionFit: String is something that ties, so in a cryptic reading it is a tier.

clue.text: Wolf's short sound effects at first well done

indicators.note: the belongings come first, placed ahead of the clipped cry

parts.note: your effects are your goods, your belongings

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: the sound a wolf makes is a howl

explanation.surface: Brief wolf noises and opening sound effects earn a congratulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wolf's' tells you whose sound is meant, and 'at first' puts the belongings ahead of the clipped cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Good show is an old-fashioned exclamation of praise, like bravo for a job done well.

clue.text: Break back in no time

parts.note: to split something is to break it
to second a proposal is to back it

explanation.surface: A bone fractures backwards in an instant.
explanation.definitionFit: A split second is an instant, practically no time at all.

clue.text: Joke store holds new sale

indicators.note: the storeroom holds the rearranged letters within it

parts.note: a pantry is a store for food

indicators.note: new signals the letters of the following word made afresh

explanation.surface: A shop is laughably running another sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'store' looks like a shop holding a sale, but it is a larder, and the anagram of the sale goes in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasantry is a light joking remark, a bit of banter.

clue.text: Criminals' lad is involved in cunning schemes

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside the schemes

parts.note: arts are wiles, cunning schemes
a son is a lad

explanation.surface: A boy gets caught up in crafty plots by crooks.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive definition stands for the plural answer as the clue's subject; arts in the sense of wiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsonists are criminals who set fire to property.

clue.text: One sort of poet ignored another's first book

indicators.note: ignored means the named letter is left out of the poet's name

parts.note: another poet here is William Blake

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A poet passes over a rival's debut volume.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove B, the first letter of 'book', from BLAKE. The Lake Poets were Wordsworth, Coleridge and Southey, who lived in England's Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake describes a particular school of poets, the Romantics of the Lake District.

clue.text: Titled heroine from log cabin?

parts.note: a heroine whose name is a book's title, and also a titled lady remembered in the diary Nelson kept in his cabin aboard Victory

explanation.walkthrough: Jane Austen's heroine names her novel; Lady Hamilton, a titled heroine, was left 'as a legacy to my country' in the codicil Nelson wrote in his cabin before Trafalgar.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen's novel takes its title from its heroine, and Lady Hamilton bore the same first name.

clue.text: Temptation in hotel room keeps one writer in a month

indicators.note: the month keeps the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Mar is the abbreviation for March
I, the Roman numeral, is one
a nib is the writing point of a pen

explanation.surface: A hotel room tempts a writer to stay for a month.
explanation.definitionFit: A minibar is a small fridge of drinks in a hotel room, tempting but pricey.

clue.text: Play's opening at length in New York, say? It depends

indicators.note: the length and the play's opening go inside the example of a state

parts.note: New York is an example of a US state

indicators.note: at means the play's opening sits next to the length abbreviation

parts.note: a play opens with Act I

explanation.surface: Whether a show's first act runs long in New York? That depends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It depends' reads as a hedge, but 'depend' also means hang down, which is what this cave formation does from the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalactite hangs from a cave roof, and to depend is an old word for to hang down.

clue.text: Film produced in a foreign country

indicators.note: the word for produced goes inside the A and the country

parts.note: the United States, foreign from a British setter's viewpoint
something produced is made

explanation.surface: A movie shot overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Amadeus is the 1984 film about Mozart.
explanation.definitionFit: Amadeus is the Oscar-winning 1984 film about Mozart and Salieri.

clue.text: Tourist, one who attempts to keep some coins

indicators.note: the attempter is made to keep the coins inside

parts.note: one who tries is a trier
pp is the abbreviation for pence, so some coins

explanation.surface: A sightseer who has a go at pocketing some small change.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripper is a tourist on a short outing, a day tripper.

clue.text: In restless state, I redesigned mansion

indicators.note: redesigned means the letters are put into a new plan

explanation.surface: Unable to sleep, I remodelled my big house.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia is the condition of being unable to sleep, a restless state.

clue.text: To the last detail, see missing summary

indicators.note: missing means the see's name is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: done precisely is done to the last detail
Ely is a cathedral city and so a bishop's see

explanation.surface: Seeing everything in detail yet missing the gist.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; ELY in Cambridgeshire is the usual crossword one.
explanation.definitionFit: A precis is a concise summary of a longer text.

clue.text: Apostle's fourth to go to a historic city

indicators.note: the fourth letter of the apostle's name is to go, removed

parts.note: Peter was one of the twelve apostles

explanation.surface: An apostle's fourth journey heads to an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: PETER drops its fourth letter, E, to give PETR, then 'to' joins A. Petra is the ruined rock city in Jordan.
explanation.definitionFit: Petra in Jordan is an ancient rock-cut city, a historic site.

clue.text: Starter that should have included egg?

definitions.text: Starter that should have included egg?

parts.words: Starter that should have included egg?
parts.note: a first course made from a nest swallows build, where you might expect to find eggs

explanation.walkthrough: The Chinese delicacy is made from the edible nests of swiftlets, so a solver muses that a nest ought to come with an egg in it.
explanation.definitionFit: This Chinese soup is served as a starter, and is made from the nests swiftlets build with saliva.

clue.text: With violence knock 7 over

indicators.note: over means turned over, the cross-referenced word read backwards

parts.note: the answer to 7 down, a word meaning ruin

explanation.surface: Hit hard, knocking the ruin over.
explanation.definitionFit: To ram is to strike with great force, a violent knock.

clue.text: Peter the Fisherman gets dirty

definitions.meaning: Britten's opera hero Peter is a fisherman of the Suffolk coast
to grime something is to blacken it with dirt

explanation.surface: A fisherman named Peter ends up filthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Britten's opera is named after its fisherman hero, and grime as a verb means to soil with dirt.

clue.text: Classic sort of lamp

definitions.meaning: a classic is a work of lasting excellence, a benchmark
a tall floor lamp is called by this name

explanation.definitionFit: A classic sets the standard, and a tall floor lamp is a standard lamp.
